title: Goods that cannot travel on Saturday
body: Yehuda is a Jewish merchant, and Saturday is his day of rest. Some of his goods must go by road on that day to reach the river boat. He asks if one of your carters can take them.

choices.label: Send your carter with the goods
choices.hint: It costs a day of your carter and 5 dinars. Yehuda will owe you a favour.

choices.label: Say you are too busy
choices.hint: Your carter earns 4 dinars on your own goods, and the street sees a house with steady work. Yehuda will ask someone else.

note: North African Jewish traders in the Geniza letters had long given goods for the road to Muslim business friends. That way no Jewish carrier had to travel on the Sabbath.

sources.at: p. 281, as quoted by Edwards and Ogilvie (2008), p. 17

title: A Christian merchant writes
body: Nicola is a Christian merchant in Alexandria. He has heard good things of your house and wants to trade with you. He asks you to send him a few bolts of linen to start.

choices.label: Send him the linen
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now and pays back 5 in three seasons. He may become a steady friend.

choices.label: Ask for a letter from someone you know
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and brings 4 dinars in three seasons. He starts with a small order.

note: Traders of different faiths had long done business together. Around 1030 one Jewish firm dealt with Christians in Alexandria, as two historians report it from Moshe Gil.

sources.at: p. 17; dealings with Christian merchants in Alexandria, citing Gil (2004), p. 687

title: A neighbour goes to Mecca
body: Hajar has saved for years to make the pilgrimage, the holy journey to Mecca. She asks to travel with your carters as far as Qus. She cannot pay much.

choices.label: Take her and pay for her food
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars, for her food and water on the road. Your street will hear of it.

choices.label: Ask a small fee for her seat
choices.hint: You are paid. Your neighbours may talk.

note: In May 1326 Ibn Battuta left Cairo for Upper Egypt, on his way to Mecca by the Red Sea road through Aydhab. A writer of the 1180s says Saladin had ended the tax on pilgrims at Aydhab.

sources.at: vol. 1, pp. 58 to 59; he left Cairo by the Upper Egypt road for the Hijaz, May 1326
p. 34; Saladin repealed the tax on pilgrims at Aydhab, from Ibn Jubayr

title: Pilgrims beg for water
body: Qasim helps pilgrims at Jeddah. It is a dry year, and the town's water must come from a day's journey away. Pilgrims are begging for it at the doors of householders.

choices.label: Pay for water carriers
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The pilgrims remember your house.

choices.label: Give a gift to the town rulers' men
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. The men are pleased, and the court hears of it.

choices.label: Send nothing
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Qasim says the pilgrims will not forget it.

note: In a dry year of Ibn Battuta's visit, water was brought to Jeddah from a day's journey away. The pilgrims begged for it from the owners of the houses.

sources.at: vol. 2, p. 360 (the year is 1328 or 1330; both in the window)

title: Litters for the emirs' wives
body: Salih makes litters, the covered seats that camels carry. The wives of some emirs, the sultan's high officers, plan to go on the Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca. They want litters from your house, and they also want to give robes to the drivers. Salih asks which litters you will rent them.

choices.label: Rent plain litters
choices.hint: The wives pay your house 3 dinars now. It is a low fee, and partners think well of your house.

choices.label: Rent showy litters
choices.hint: The wives pay your house 8 dinars now. People complain of the show, and the court hears of it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The court sees that you stayed clear.

note: In 1346 the wives of some emirs went on the Hajj with litters so grand that people complained. They gave robes to camel riders and water carriers, and the chief judge spoke against them in his sermon.

title: A city of two halves
body: A neighbour at Galata says the city is divided. Galata is the quarter kept for the Franks: Genoese, Venetians, men of Rome and French. He asks which side you will buy from.

choices.label: Deal with the Italian quarter
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. Prices are steady, and foreign houses think well of you.

choices.label: Deal with the Greeks of the old city
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. It is cheaper, and partners like it.

choices.label: Deal with both
choices.hint: It costs 9 dinars now. The risk is spread, and the court hears of it.

note: Galata was set aside for Franks, who paid the king a yearly tax but often rebelled. Ibn Battuta wrote this about 1332, and his editor says it was really a Genoese colony.

title: A go-between for pepper
body: A Venetian friend may not trade with Egypt, because the pope has forbidden it. He asks you to find a Greek merchant of Cyprus to carry his pepper.

choices.label: Find the go-between
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now, a fee for the go-between. The Venetians remember.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The Venetian buys through a rival.

choices.label: Carry it yourself
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. You carry his pepper to Cyprus, and he pays you 12 dinars in two seasons, more than the Greek would earn. The court may frown on it, and partners like the profit.

note: Greeks in Cyprus felt the pope's ban on trade with Egypt did not bind them, so they acted as agents for Venetians. This is told of the years after 1291.

title: Oil in new barrels
body: A buyer at Tunis wants olive oil, but only in new barrels. Old barrels may have held wine or fat, and then the court could refuse the oil.

choices.label: Pay for new barrels
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. The oil is accepted, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Ship it in old barrels
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and 6 dinars in two seasons, a fine if the court refuses it. Your people save the cost of barrels.

choices.label: Sell the oil in Cairo instead
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. The price is lower, and partners think it careful.

note: Pegolotti says oil sent to Tunis should come in new barrels. Old ones might have held wine, fat or pork, and then the court could refuse the oil and fine the merchant.

title: Goods with the pilgrims
body: A pilgrim caravan is leaving Damascus for the Hijaz. A neighbour suggests sending a few loads of your goods with it. Pilgrim caravans often pay fewer tolls.

choices.label: Send the goods with the pilgrims
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. There are few tolls, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Keep them for a trade caravan
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now, the full tolls. The court notes that you pay.

choices.label: Send a pilgrim with money for the road
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. Foreign houses hear of your gift.

note: Ibn Battuta wrote that the pilgrim caravan left Damascus at the new moon of Shawwal, on 1 September 1326 by Gibb's count. Gibb notes that such caravans were often free of the usual road and customs duties.
